author: @jeremyfowers

evidence.api_compatibility: No breaking API change. The new GPUInfo.driver_missing field is a new optional boolean added to the struct, defaulting to false. The llamacpp:cuda state values 'unsupported' and 'action_required' are new states for scenarios where the backend was previously unavailable anyway. The auto default for llamacpp may shift from cuda to vulkan on a system where CUDA was silently failing, which improves rather than breaks the user experience.
evidence.documentation: docs/guide/configuration/llamacpp.md was updated with driver requirements, minimum driver versions, and a note about CUDA minor-version compatibility. The commit message is detailed with tables. The PR body was generated by Claude Code and contains a TODO placeholder in the summary section, which violates the project's ai-content-policy requiring human-written PR bodies.
evidence.manual_release_testing: The behavior is user-visible: on a system with an NVIDIA GPU but no NVIDIA driver installed, llamacpp:cuda reports 'unsupported (NVIDIA driver not installed or not loaded)' and auto falls through to Vulkan. A system with a driver older than 528.33 (Windows) or 525.60.13 (Linux) sees 'action_required' with the driver download link. These paths have not been shown to be exercised by a human on real hardware; CI uses mock device data.
evidence.post_approval_commits: No commits were added after the approval at 2026-11-05T16:21:04Z. The last author commit (cfee3b0625) was at 2026-11-05T15:50:15Z, over 30 minutes before approval. This is clean.
evidence.review: The PR received one human review from @fl0rianr (submitted 2026-11-05T14:37:19Z, state CHANGES_REQUESTED). @fl0rianr identified two focused P1 issues: (1) nvidia_driver_block() gated Vulkan rows that list nvidia_gpu alongside other devices, and (2) an unsupported architecture (e.g. Pascal sm_61) on an old driver was incorrectly upgraded from 'unsupported' to 'action_required'. Both were fixed in subsequent commits (8213156, cd016f8). @fl0rianr then approved at 2026-11-05T16:21:04Z with 'LGTM'. @fl0rianr's subject areas (LMX, GUI, CI, smart router) do not include CUDA, system info, or llamacpp; per docs/dev/contribute.md, the subject-area reviewers for these areas are @kenvandine (Nvidia CUDA) and @superm1 (system info, llamacpp). Neither was pinged, so no reviewer with subject-matter expertise reviewed this PR. Despite this gap, the review was technically sharp and the author addressed every finding before approval.
evidence.security: No security concerns. The change adds driver-version detection logic (reading /sys/class/drm/device/driver on Linux, Win32_PnPEntity on Windows) and compares version strings. No network calls, credential handling, or code execution paths are introduced. The NVIDIA driver download URL is a static constant.
evidence.tests: A new test file test/cpp/test_nvidia_driver_gating.cpp with 221 lines adds 8 test functions covering: current driver passes, missing driver blocks, old driver requires action, unreadable driver version is not gated, Vulkan fallback stays available, unsupported arch is preserved, and missing driver with unknown arch names the driver. Unit tests in test_system_info_helpers.cpp cover nvidia_driver_older_than (9 checks) and nvidia_driver_version_from_windows / cuda_min_driver_version (8 checks). The detector-level logic in WindowsSystemInfo::get_nvidia_gpu_devices and LinuxSystemInfo::get_nvidia_gpu_devices has no direct test — the gating test mocks driver_missing directly. All CI checks passed (C++ Server Build, PPA, Validate New llama.cpp Release).

maintainer_todos.text: Replace the PR body summary with a human-written sentence explaining what the PR changes, why the minimum driver versions were chosen, and how a user sees the result.

Run lemond on a system with an NVIDIA GPU and either no driver or an old driver (e.g. 516.94 on Windows, 515.105.01 on Linux), open the web UI or query the device info endpoint, and confirm that llamacpp:cuda reports 'unsupported' or 'action_required' with the correct message and that auto backend selection falls through to Vulkan.

subject: Gate NVIDIA CUDA backends on a missing or outdated driver (#4066)
summary: Adds NVIDIA driver-missing and driver-too-old gating to llamacpp:cuda — a missing driver reports 'unsupported' and falls through to Vulkan as the auto default; a driver older than the CUDA 12.0 floor (528.33 on Windows, 525.60.13 on Linux) reports 'action_required' with a driver download link; sd-cpp:cuda, Vulkan rows, and unsupported-architecture rows are left unaffected.
verdict_reason: The commit introduces user-visible driver-gating behavior that has not been shown to be exercised by a human on real hardware.
